claims.title: How much of the torsion lies at each geometric point?
claims.hypotheses: The unitary abelian variety has algebra degree one over an algebraically closed residue field, with the admissible prime-to-q principal level and a chosen coefficient place of residue cardinality Q. The ideal-torsion degree theorem applies.
claims.statement: If M is the number of geometric points of the distinguished torsion and ℓ the local length at its identity, then Q^n=Mℓ, M=Q^j and ℓ=Q^(n−j).

claims.title: Why does the tangent at the identity force a dichotomy?
claims.hypotheses: The unitary datum of algebra degree one has the prescribed Lie signature and separated coefficient places.
claims.statement: The tangent space of the distinguished torsion at the identity is a line. The local length is either Q, giving Q^(n−1) points, or at least Q².

claims.title: How does the local length give a coordinate for the torsion?
claims.hypotheses: B is a finite-dimensional commutative local k-algebra with the given residue field k and a one-dimensional tangent space.
claims.statement: Any generator of the cotangent line gives B ≅ k[X]/(X^ℓ), where ℓ is the local length. If ℓ>Q this yields a quotient to k[t]/(t^(Q+1)).

claims.title: Where does the first derivative go under a Qth power?
claims.hypotheses: The field k has prime characteristic q, Q=q^f with f positive, and the torsion ring has local length greater than Q and a one-dimensional tangent space.
claims.statement: The Q-power endomorphism of the truncated test ring factors as restriction to the dual numbers followed by an injective ring map. The torsion test point restricts to a nonzero tangent.

claims.title: What happens to the lifted tangent after Frobenius?
claims.hypotheses: The unitary coefficient congruence and projected Hodge character line hold over the algebraically closed residue field. A nonzero tangent comes from the lifted point killed by the distinguished ideal.
claims.statement: The chosen coefficient isogeny factors through f iterates of Frobenius. The residual semilinear group morphism sends the lifted tangent to the image of the constant tangent.

claims.title: Which Hodge classes does the constant tangent detect?

claims.title: Which eigenvector can a functional separate from the Frobenius image?
claims.hypotheses: The commuting coefficient actions preserve the Hodge filtration, the projected Hodge line is a nonzero character line killed by Frobenius, and the local coefficient congruences, nilpotence and annihilator relations hold.
claims.statement: There is a simultaneous character eigenvector in the coefficient image outside the span of the weighted Frobenius image. A linear functional fixed by the dual projector vanishes on that span and takes value one at this vector.
